question:
For every $x\in[-1,1]$, a mathematics group defines $S(x)=\sin^{-1}x+\cos^{-1}x$. Although the two inverse functions have different principal ranges, their sum satisfies a standard inverse-trigonometric property. The group first evaluates the expression at a particular value and then establishes its general behaviour. This allows the students to determine whether $S$ varies with $x$ and to identify its range without drawing a graph.

(a) Evaluate $S\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$.

(b) Establish the value of $S(x)$ for an arbitrary $x\in[-1,1]$.

(c) Determine the range of $S$.

(d) Evaluate $3S(x)-\pi$ and justify why its value is independent of $x$.
explanation:
(a)
Using principal values, $$\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{\pi}{6}$$ and $$\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{\pi}{3}$$ Therefore, $$S\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{\pi}{2}$$

(b)
The applicable property is $$\sin^{-1}x+\cos^{-1}x=\frac{\pi}{2},\quad -1\leq x\leq1$$ Hence, $S(x)=\frac{\pi}{2}$ for every admissible $x$.

(c)
Since $S(x)$ has the same value $\frac{\pi}{2}$ for every $x\in[-1,1]$, its range contains exactly one value. Therefore, the range is $\left\{\frac{\pi}{2}\right\}$.

(d)
Substituting $S(x)=\frac{\pi}{2}$ gives $$3S(x)-\pi=3\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)-\pi=\frac{\pi}{2}$$ The inverse-trigonometric property makes $S(x)$ constant, so $3S(x)-\pi$ is also independent of $x$.

options.D:
(a) $S\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

(b) $S(x)=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ for every $x\in[-1,1]$

(c) Range: $\left\{\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right\}$

(d) $3S(x)-\pi=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, independent of $x$ because $S$ is constant
